title: Every reward payment must be recorded against a transaction hash in a fixed six-field schema
content:
Each third-party Instance defines a Payment Details Per Reward Period document (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.2.3.3.5.0.6.1 and siblings) as "a table where each entry represents a single payment," with six mandatory fields: Reward Period, Payee, Payment Address, Amount Paid, Transaction Hash, Transaction Date.

Specifying the schema — rather than just requiring records — is what gives the provision force. Amount Paid alone is a claim; Amount Paid plus Payment Address plus Transaction Hash is a claim that any observer can independently verify against the chain, without cooperation from Skybase or the partner.

Reward Period ties the payment back to the measurement window defined by the Instance's Tracking Methodology, closing the loop between what was attributed and what was paid. Together the fields make the two halves of the reward program — measurement and settlement — reconcilable to each other rather than merely both documented.

Combined with the Active Data designation on these tables, the result is a governed schema with an operational writer: Operational GovOps may add rows by Direct Edit, but cannot change what a row must contain, since the schema itself sits in a `[Core]` document. That split is what lets the record stay current without letting the standard of proof drift.
description: Reward Period, Payee, Payment Address, Amount Paid, Transaction Hash and Transaction Date make each payment reconcilable on-chain by construction rather than by later audit request.
